_comment: Machine-parseable registry of all best-practices rubrics. Consume this to discover rubrics, check adoption, and validate system scores. See README.md for dimension-type conventions. The optional `foundation` field on a rubric links it to its theory doc in foundations/; scripts/check-foundations-coverage.py gates that every foundations/*.md has exactly one rubric pointing back to it.

critics.lens: PEV loop, harness quality, vanilla > ceremony
Platform vs. product, N=20+ coordination, API surface
Trust boundaries, lethal trifecta, structural injection defense
Make illegal states unrepresentable, type-driven design, signature honesty
Workflows vs. agents (the determinism boundary), tool contracts, measured failure modes
Reproducibility, automated deployment pipeline, idempotency, testability = determinism

dimension_types.gate: Scoreable mechanically — routing F1, pass/fail, counts, linter output. Can be an automated CI check.
dimension_types.review: Requires expert human judgment — quality of verify target, inversion completeness, discoverability.
dimension_types.hypothesis: Stated as an observable property but not yet empirically verified across invocations. Track with timing data.

rubrics.name: skills-holistic
rubrics.key_question: Does this skill address all ten load-bearing quality dimensions — instructions, control mode, rubrics, mechanization, evaluation, extensibility, security, observability, context engineering, and plan anatomy?
rubrics.note: Meta-rubric synthesizing all ten load-bearing skill quality dimensions. Use at creation time (does this new skill address all 10?) and at evaluation time (does this existing skill score holistically?). Individual dimension rubrics provide drill-down detail. D9 (Context Engineering) and D10 (Plan Anatomy) were promoted from cross-cutting rubrics in v0.2.0; governance stays cross-cutting (team/system scale) — see the rubric's §Scope.
rubrics.empirical_application_notes: First application 2026-05-31 (v0.2.0): fresh-context dogfood scoring core-agent-loops v0.1.7 — core-agent-loops/reviews/2026-05-31-holistic-10dim-dogfood-scorecard.md. D9/D10 discriminated; the run surfaced a novel Critical two prior 9-critic panels missed (now fixed in core-agent-loops v0.1.8).

rubrics.name: harness-design
rubrics.key_question: What belongs in AGENTS.md, and what does bloat look like?

rubrics.name: agentic-coding
rubrics.key_question: Does this system close the Plan→Execute→Verify loop reliably?

rubrics.name: prompt-control-modes
rubrics.key_question: Does the prompt's control mode match the task's entropy, risk, and desired autonomy?

rubrics.name: context-engineering
rubrics.key_question: Is context a precision instrument or a dumping ground?

rubrics.name: skills-authoring
rubrics.key_question: Does this skill compound over invocations, or accumulate drift?

rubrics.name: tool-use
rubrics.key_question: Are tools contracts with clear success criteria, or guesses with side effects?

rubrics.name: evaluation-workflows
rubrics.key_question: Are systems tested adversarially with fresh context, or self-confirmed by their builders?

rubrics.name: inversion-and-abstraction
rubrics.key_question: Is the agent deciding and observing, or manually executing what a script should do?

rubrics.name: progressive-context-construction
rubrics.key_question: Does context grow with the task, or arrive fully-formed as noise before the first action?

rubrics.name: multi-agent-coordination
rubrics.key_question: Is agent isolation structural or behavioral — and what happens when behavioral contracts break?

rubrics.name: observability-and-telemetry
rubrics.key_question: Can you answer the 5-minute test from telemetry, or is all analysis anecdotal?

rubrics.name: generative-ui-reasoning
rubrics.key_question: Does the agent reason top-down from intent to decision before emitting components, or does it prematurely render?

rubrics.name: security-and-scope-containment
rubrics.key_question: Does agent privilege match task scope, and is the lethal trifecta structurally prevented?

rubrics.name: mechanization-best-practices
rubrics.key_question: Are repeatable, testable, failure-prone procedures moved out of prose into deterministic mechanisms — and chosen at the right enforcement level (script / validator / hook / CI gate / workflow / policy)?

rubrics.name: skill-extensibility
rubrics.key_question: Does the skill learn from observed evidence without bloating the cold-start surface — with placement discipline, regression safety, and a closed observe → classify → place → verify → monitor → prune/promote/mechanize loop?

rubrics.name: worktree-operations
rubrics.key_question: Is multi-agent Git/worktree state typed and bounded — with manifest-backed lifecycle, path ownership, validation gates, and recovery protocol — or is integration a conflict-accumulation lane?

rubrics.name: agents-ux-wireframing-ascii
rubrics.key_question: Does the agent produce an ASCII wireframe (structural reasoning artifact) between intent and implementation — covering region traceability, ownership, state, and responsive behavior — or does it collapse directly from prompt to polished components?

rubrics.name: prd-authoring
rubrics.key_question: Does the PRD establish shared product intent for the human team — problem, users, outcomes, scope boundaries, tradeoffs — without collapsing into a disguised implementation plan or a vague feature list?

rubrics.name: spec-authoring
rubrics.key_question: Does the SPEC define an execution contract bounded enough for a coding agent to implement, verify, and stop safely — or does it leave ambiguity that the agent fills with its own assumptions, producing over-edits, under-implementations, or unsafe refactors?

rubrics.name: composite-css-composition-discipline
rubrics.key_question: When an agent composes UI from primitives + composites with their own @scope CSS, does it respect the layered contracts (composition grammars, intrinsic display, slot vocabularies) or override them in ways that silently break the child's intrinsic layout?

rubrics.name: report-authoring
rubrics.key_question: Does the report give its reader a trustworthy, decision-ready picture — every claim traceable to a named source, signals calibrated and honest, the bottom line first, and ingested material treated as data rather than instructions — or is it a well-formatted document whose assertions cannot be verified?
rubrics.source: Derived 2026-05-31 from the report-* family review (4 blind skills-studio passes that converged on these dimensions).

rubrics.name: plan-anatomy
rubrics.key_question: Are the agent's plans well-structured bridges from intent to reliable execution — verifiable subgoals, explicit dependencies, checkpoints before expensive steps, real-state completion criteria, recovery paths — or vague sequences the model improvises through, producing different execution paths from identical inputs?

rubrics.name: governance
rubrics.key_question: Does the system have explicit governance — change control, eval governance, role separation, audit trails, policy-as-code, and override authority — or does it rely on informal norms and govern by whoever-happened-to-make-the-change?

rubrics.name: cold-start-orientation
rubrics.key_question: Can a first-time user answer 'use [skill]' and 'how should I use [skill]?' helpfully from SKILL.md alone, without loading reference files or reading beyond line 50?

rubrics.name: rubric-quality
rubrics.key_question: Does this rubric produce consistent, calibrated scores — or does it generate noise through adjective-only anchors, mislabeled criteria, and unverified hypotheses asserted as facts?

rubrics.name: expert-council-design
rubrics.key_question: Is the skill's panel of critics/personas a well-designed instrument — voices grounded in verifiable authority, the set partitioning the space without redundancy, persona the right control mode, output falsifiable, and the panel proven to discriminate a failing artifact, not only bless good ones?
rubrics.source: Derived 2026-05-31 from the brand-studio re-review (skills-studio dogfood) — no home existed for scoring the critic panel a skill ships, distinct from the rubrics it ships.

rubrics.name: runtime-compatibility
rubrics.description: Validates runtime target (agent/chat/both), tool usage consistency, §SelfAudit gates, artifact sandbox safety, graceful degradation, and MCP documentation.
rubrics.load_when: Always during score/promote — prerequisite gate before D1-D10. Also when authoring to validate target declaration.

adoption_contract._comment: Systems adopting these rubrics should declare which rubrics they implement and their current scores. This enables automated adoption tracking and regression detection.
